why_current_code_is_racy: createBatchStore.transaction() performs readState(target), clones the whole JSON state, mutates the clone, then replaces the whole file with writeAtomic().
writeAtomic() makes each replacement crash-safer, but it does not serialize two independent read-modify-write transactions across processes.

Therefore two writers can both read the same old state, commit different updates, and the later whole-file replacement silently erases the earlier update even when the writers touch different batches/tasks.

offline_reproduction.mechanism: Two child processes intentionally capture the same pre-commit whole-file snapshot. Process A commits task-a=running first; process B then commits its stale snapshot with task-b=running.

candidate_contract_probe.mechanism: Serialize the complete read-modify-write interval across processes before either reader takes its snapshot.

safety_impact: The persisted coding-subagent state is the restart/retry safety boundary for pending/running/uncertain/done work. Losing an unrelated writer's update can make the durable state disagree with work that actually happened.
This is broader than the already-recorded same-task concurrent-claim race: even different batches or different task ids share one JSON file and can overwrite each other.

A future Notion->Qwen adapter increases the chance of concurrent independent delegated jobs reaching the same global store, so fixing only same-task claim ownership would not close this store-wide race.
required_fix_contract: Serialize the entire store transaction across processes, including the initial read, mutation, and durable replace; locking only writeAtomic() is insufficient.
The mechanism must be crash-safe and bounded: a dead process must not leave an unrecoverable permanent lock.
Atomic claim/compare-and-swap for one task must use the same serialization/versioning domain as all other batch-store mutations, otherwise unrelated writes can still erase it.
Add a regression with two processes updating different batches from the same initial snapshot and require both updates to survive.
Add a second regression where one process persists uncertain/done while another updates an unrelated task; the terminal/uncertain state must never roll back to stale running/pending.
